scope: Read-only functional audit; isolated debug/test instrumentation, no deployed app changes, no submission.

findings.title: Changing bike stations can leave navigation disabled without recovery
findings.user_effect: After selecting an alternative pickup, the ETA disappears and Start navigation is disabled even though loading has stopped.
findings.cause: moveBikeStation accepts the result of cycle without checking updated.verified; cycle can return a leg with duration nil. There is no retry/recovery state.
findings.remedy: Commit a replacement only after its route is verified; otherwise preserve a usable state and offer retry or another station.

findings.title: Slower cycling displaces faster transit
findings.user_effect: A 15-minute bike trip is placed ahead of a 7-minute bus trip because it beats a 25-minute walk.
findings.cause: beatsTransit OR beatsWalking inserts cycling at index 0, bypassing comparative ranking.
findings.remedy: Separate eligibility from ranking; retain bike alternatives without placing dominated trips first.

findings.title: Past pickup stations still interrupt riding and the final walk
findings.user_effect: After taking a bike, and after entering the final walk, the app still warns that the original pickup has no bikes.
findings.cause: bikeAlert checks only whether the entire leg has passed; it does not use cyclingPhase.
findings.control_passed: A full upcoming dropoff correctly warns during riding.
findings.remedy: Tie pickup/return checks to confirmed trip progress; ignore stations already served.

findings.title: Cycling uses pedestrian directions without cycling suitability checks
findings.user_effect: The green ride path is a walking path timed at cycling speed; it has not been verified as suitable for bicycles. Turn instructions are also dropped.
evidence: cycle calls walk for the ridden segment
walk requests MKDirections walking transport type
findings.remedy: Use bicycle-suitable routing or distinguish dismount/walking sections and preserve instructions; validate real street cases.

findings.title: Compressed travel-time download and backup are not deployed
findings.user_effect: The app falls back to the 26,250,699-byte full file; GitHub loss has no working travel-time mirror.
findings.remedy: Publish the verified compressed data and manifest to both configured sources, then check them as part of health monitoring.

findings.title: Current shared configuration is rejected by installed 1.8.0
findings.user_effect: 1.8.0 keeps old/default settings instead of applying the new quick update.
findings.cause: Strict decoder rejects new planning.bikeWalkGainSeconds while the feed declares minimumAppVersion 1.1.8.
findings.control: Removing only bikeWalkGainSeconds allows the actual 1.8.0 decoder to accept the same document.
findings.remedy: Keep the shared feed compatible with shipped decoders or serve version-specific settings; 1.8.1 already has a 120-second default.

initial_pro.reason: First route changed during street verification; fixed test wait and retested successfully.

reasons: City bus tap selected a metro train instead; bus camera round-trip not established.
Simulator could not terminate the app before the dense-fleet test.

focused_retry.manual_review_note: Replacement test did not assert Start navigation remains enabled. Manual screenshot and state review exposed the disabled-start defect.

limitations: No physical-device road test or physical frame-rate measurement.
Fixed planner fixtures reproduce logic behavior; they are not actual published bus arrival forecasts.
The city-overview bus selection/return camera case remains unverified; do not claim all camera animations or real-device frame rates passed.
visual_notes: English long stop names are truncated in compact navigation banners, while Chinese counterparts remain visible.
The orange interface-test banners in screenshots identify simulated test data and are not part of production UI.
